rulings.matter: 1 -- are RUL-0001's four blocking conditions discharged
rulings.ruling:
ALL FOUR ARE DISCHARGED, AND I VERIFIED EACH AGAINST THE TREE RATHER THAN AGAINST THE REPORT THAT WAS HANDED TO ME. I state the instrument for each, because a condition cleared by reading a summary of the tree is not cleared.

(1) CRITERION 7 EVIDENCE -- DISCHARGED. Studio/evidence/tests/EVD-0010.json exists: tier T0, taskId WO-0008, commit 4f4135e, producedBy core-simulation-engineer, and its summary inlines runner text for four tests including 'Failed Regression_NaNDtLeavesElapsedSecondsFiniteAndUnchanged [1 ms] Expected: True But was: False'. That is captured NUnit output in NUnit's own idiom, not the composed narrative RUL-0004 matter 2b caught in the WO-0009 markdown, and the record says so itself. Criterion 7's own wording -- 'a regression test that never demonstrably failed does not satisfy this criterion' -- is now met on its own terms.

(2) CRITERION 11 BUILD-AND-SUITE EVIDENCE -- DISCHARGED. EVD-0011.json: tier T1, taskId WO-0008, commit 4f4135e, buildWarnings 0, coreTests 180, kernelTests 162. RUL-0001 asked for 'all 146 tests'; the record reports 180, which is more rather than fewer and is consistent with two later orders having added tests. A record exists where none existed, which is what the condition asked for.

(3) CRITERION 6 AMENDED BY ITS AUTHOR -- DISCHARGED, AND DONE WELL. WO-0008's criterion 6 now carries the domain bound RUL-0001 matter 1 specified: the exact real-valued sum of accepted dt must not exceed float.MaxValue, and a sequence exceeding it is 'outside this criterion's domain and neither satisfies nor violates it'. The finiteness requirement, its scope over throwing and no-op calls, and its parenthetical are unchanged. The order's rationale records the amendment, cites RUL-0001 matter 1 and PRO-0004, quotes the ORIGINAL criterion 6 text verbatim so a later reader can see what changed, and states that no other criterion is touched. That is the amendment discipline RUL-0003 matter 3 demanded of WO-0010, produced here by the same author without being asked twice. I record it as the studio's good precedent and I refer to it again in RUL-0007.

(4) Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote REWRITTEN -- DISCHARGED. Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:306-327 now ticks float.MaxValue / 2f twice and asserts float.IsFinite is true and ElapsedSeconds equals float.MaxValue. That is exactly the replacement RUL-0001 matter 2 authorised, element for element: the negated Is.False on float.IsFinite is gone, the boundary of the amended criterion is pinned in its place, and the comment reasons down from the specification rather than up from the code. The test that punished the fix no longer exists.

I ALSO CHECKED THE CONDITION RUL-0001 DID NOT PUT IN ITS BLOCKING LIST, because leaving it out looks like an oversight rather than a decision. RUL-0001's fourth matter named a gate step in prose: someone with a shell must run `git diff ae3169b -- Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateVerificationTests.cs` and confirm only the three authorised hunks plus the added regression test. It is unrecorded. See matter 3; it is the same gap as WO-0009's, and I am not letting it through on either order.

NO, AND NOT FOR ANY REASON TO DO WITH THE ENGINEERING, WHICH IS FINISHED. I refuse closure on one ground that is common to both orders and decisive on its own: THE GATE VERDICT THAT CLOSURE MUST NAME DOES NOT EXIST.

This is a kernel fact, not a standard I invented for this adjudication. Studio/kernel/schemas/gate.schema.json defines a gate-verdict as a first-class record: kind 'gate-verdict', gate, TASKID, verdict, evaluatedAt, evaluatedBy, evidence. It is keyed to a work order. task.schema.json says 'A task is only complete when a gate said so', and completedByGate is a gateId -- a pointer. The thing it points at, in this kernel's own vocabulary, is a gate-verdict record naming this taskId. I searched the repository. The string 'gate-verdict' occurs in exactly five files: gate.schema.json, two invalid kernel fixtures, and the two valid fixtures gate.verdict-pass.json and gate.verdict-fail.json, the first of which is a pass for the imaginary WO-0142. There is no live gate-verdict record anywhere in this studio -- not for WO-0008, not for WO-0009, not for any order it has ever run. Studio/state has directories for events, escalations, reports, proposals, rulings and challenges, and none for gate verdicts.

I was told G2 CI run 58 reports success on commit 13900d3, which carries all of the above. I cannot check that and I will not pretend otherwise: I have no shell, no git and no CI access in this environment, and the repository contains no mention of run 58 or of commit 13900d3 anywhere -- I grepped the whole tree for both. My only route to that fact is the word of the agent that dispatched me. WRITING completedByGate: 'G2' ON THE STRENGTH OF AN AGENT TELLING ME A GATE PASSED IS SELF-CERTIFICATION WITH ONE EXTRA HOP IN IT. The record would then say a gate said so, when what actually happened is that an agent said so and an adjudicator transcribed it. That is the precise motion the architecture exists to refuse, and it does not become acceptable because the underlying claim is probably true.

Three further reasons this is not pedantry, in ascending order.

First, a CI run evaluates a COMMIT; a gate verdict rules on an ORDER. Run 58 does not know WO-0008 exists. It cannot attest that criterion 7's regression test is the one EVD-0010 reddened, that criterion 6's amendment was authorised by RUL-0001 rather than fitted to the code, or that the twelve criteria are the twelve criteria. That binding -- gate result to taskId to the evidence ids carrying the order-specific claims -- is exactly what the gateVerdict record's required fields are for, and it is the binding that is missing. A green commit plus an adjudicator's confidence is not a substitute for it; it is the thing the record was designed to replace.

Second, no evidence record ties a green build-and-suite run to 13900d3. EVD-0011 is at 4f4135e. The evidence schema requires a commit for every automated tier, and its stated reason is that evidence which cannot be tied to a state of the code cannot be reasoned about later. If run 58 is the gate evaluation, then the state of the code it judged is currently unrecorded, and closure would cite a commit that appears nowhere in the studio's own record.

Third, G2's owner is 'ci' and its overridableBy is the empty array, enforced by the schema itself. I am not entitled to supply this verdict and neither is my dispatcher by reporting one. That is the whole content of 'I may never override gate G2': not merely that I may not wave a failure through, but that I may not manufacture a pass.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS, AND IT IS CHEAP. A gate-verdict record for WO-0008 -- kind 'gate-verdict', gate 'G2', taskId 'WO-0008', verdict 'pass', evaluatedAt, evaluatedBy 'ci', evidence ['EVD-0010','EVD-0011'] -- filed by or on behalf of G2's owner and carrying the commit it was evaluated at. Then completedByGate: 'G2' points at something, and I will close the order on the next pass without re-adjudicating anything in matter 1. I am refusing a missing artefact, not the work.

I RECORD PLAINLY THAT THIS GAP IS NOT THE IMPLEMENTER'S FAULT AND NOT THIS ROUND'S. It has been open since the studio started and nobody noticed because no order had ever reached the point of closing. WO-0008 is the first order to arrive at the gate with its conditions actually discharged, and it has discovered that the last link in the chain of custody was never built. That is a finding worth having, and it belongs to me rather than to engineering: designing the closure path is an architecture decision and those are mine. The correct reading of this ruling is that WO-0008 is done and the studio is not yet able to say so.

rulings.matter: 3 -- the unrecorded diff, on both orders
rulings.ruling:
BLOCKING, AND I AM SAYING SO ON WO-0008 EVEN THOUGH RUL-0001 LEFT IT OUT OF ITS BLOCKING LIST, BECAUSE THE OMISSION WAS A CONTAINER PROBLEM AND NOT A JUDGEMENT.

RUL-0001 matter 4 states it explicitly: 'I am naming that as a gate step, not claiming it as done' -- the step being `git diff ae3169b -- Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateVerificationTests.cs`, confirming only the three authorised hunks plus the added regression test. WO-0008 criterion 8 ends 'No other existing assertion in this file is altered', which is a claim about a diff and is checkable no other way. Nothing in Studio/evidence, Studio/state or anywhere else in the repository records that diff having been run: I grepped the evidence tree for 'diff', 'untouched' and 'unchanged' and the only hit is an unrelated line in EVD-0007.

I note what IS mechanically covered, so that the condition is not read as broader than it is. Studio/build/check-forbidden-remedies.sh check 3 counts Assert./Assume. occurrences per file against the merge base and fails if a file lost any, and gate-g2.sh runs it. If run 58 is green, then no file under Assets/Tests LOST an assertion. That covers 'removed'. It does not cover 'altered' or 'weakened' -- an assertion whose expected value changed keeps its count. So the mechanical check discharges roughly a third of what criterion 8 claims, and the diff discharges the rest.

This is the second consecutive order on which a director named a diff as a gate step and nobody performed it, and it composes with matter 2: the natural home for the result is the gate-verdict record's evidence list, via a T0 record carrying the diff output. One artefact closes both.

IT MUST BE RENAMED, THE RENAME IS AUTHORISED HERE, AND IT MUST HAPPEN BEFORE THE GATE VERDICT IS TAKEN RATHER THAN AFTER.

The agent was right not to rename it unasked, and I want that recorded before I overrule the consequence. RUL-0001 matter 2 authorised a replacement of the test's body, scoped 'to exactly this one test and nothing else in the file'. A rename is not a replacement of a body, and an implementer who reads an authorisation narrowly and stops at its edge is doing the thing this studio keeps asking for. The defect is in my predecessors' authorisation, not in the agent's reading of it.

But the name now lies about the body, and it lies in the studio's most-repeated failure shape. RUL-0001 matter 3(b) recorded Criterion10_RunStateDoesNotReferenceDeltaTime as a test that 'promised in its name what its body never looked at'. This is the mirror image: the body is now correct and the name promises the opposite of what it does. A test called OverflowPossibilityNote that in fact asserts NO overflow occurs at the boundary is worse than a merely vague name -- a future reader searching for what pins the overflow behaviour will find it, read the name, and draw the inverted conclusion. RUL-0001 ordered this test rewritten precisely because it was 'a standing instruction to the next reader that overflowing the run clock is required behaviour'. Half of that instruction is still standing, in the identifier.

DISPOSITION. I adopt qa-director's own precedent from RUL-0004, which handled this correctly for Criterion10_MultipleFairingPaths and whose reasoning I quote because it is exactly right: 'A rename changes no assertion; it is named here only so the change is traceable to a ruling rather than appearing as an unattributed edit.' So: rename authorised, to a name that states what the test pins -- criterion 6's amended boundary, that ElapsedSeconds stays finite and exact when the sum of accepted dt reaches float.MaxValue. I deliberately do not dictate the string. Naming a test is close enough to authoring one that I would rather leave it to the agent with the write scope and be sure I stayed on my side of the line.

WHY IT IS BLOCKING RATHER THAN LOGGED, WHICH IS THE ONLY PART OF THIS THAT NEEDS DEFENDING. A rename cannot change the suite's outcome and on its own would not be worth holding an order for. It is blocking because of WHEN, not what. Assets/Tests/Core.Tests is in WO-0008's write scope while WO-0008 is open; the moment the order closes, this file is inside no open order's scope and this authorisation has outlived the order that carried it. An authorised-but-unmade correction that survives its own order becomes exactly the unattributed edit RUL-0004's reasoning exists to prevent, and the next agent to touch the file will either make it without cover or leave it. Since I am already holding both orders for matter 2, folding this in costs nothing and it must land inside the same commit the gate verdict is taken on. If it slips, it is not to be made afterwards on the strength of this paragraph -- it comes back to me.

rulings.matter: 5 -- criterion 6's amendment, checked for the motion RUL-0003 refused
rulings.ruling:
IT IS A NARROWING OF DOMAIN AND NOT A NARROWING OF THE SAFETY CLAIM, AND I CHECKED THAT MYSELF RATHER THAN INHERITING IT, BECAUSE I AM THE DIRECTOR WHO DREW THAT LINE IN RUL-0003 AND IT WOULD BE CHEAP TO APPLY IT ONLY TO OTHER PEOPLE'S ORDERS.

RUL-0003 matter 2 refused option (b) on WO-0010 -- amending a criterion to the range over which the code happens to work -- on the ground that amending a SATISFIABLE criterion to fit an implementation is the same motion as weakening an assertion. Criterion 6 here looks superficially similar and is not, on the distinction RUL-0003 matter 3 drew and which I now apply against my own precedent.

WO-0010's criterion 11 was satisfiable: an implementation existed that met it as written, so the defect was against the criterion. WO-0008's criterion 6 was UNSATISFIABLE, and unsatisfiable jointly with criterion 5 of the same order, which mandates that float.MaxValue be accepted and added. Two such accepted calls sum to 6.805e38 against a binary32 maximum of 3.4028235e38 and store as +Infinity; every dt in that sequence is finite and non-negative, nothing throws, nothing is a no-op, so the sequence satisfies criterion 6's precondition and violates its conclusion under the behaviour criterion 5 requires. No conforming implementation can satisfy both. That is a defect IN the criterion, and RUL-0001 graded it unsatisfiableAsWritten and raised PRO-0004, which is the schema's own required route for exactly this case.

And the direction of the amendment is right. It does not say ElapsedSeconds stays finite over a smaller range while leaving inputs on which it silently goes infinite -- that would be option (b)'s shape. It removes from the criterion's domain the sequences the criterion could never have coherently described, and it says so in terms: such a sequence 'neither satisfies nor violates it'. The finiteness guarantee over every sequence the criterion still claims is unchanged and unweakened. The overflow itself remains an acceptable documented limit rather than a certified behaviour -- float.MaxValue is on the order of 1e31 years of run time -- and, importantly, the rewritten test now pins the amended boundary from the SAFE side rather than pinning the overflow. Criterion 6 as amended is true. Criterion 6 as written was false. That is the correct direction of travel and I ratify it.

criteriaAssessment.notes: Criteria 1-5, 9, 10 and 12 are ADOPTED from RUL-0001 and not independently re-derived. RUL-0001 graded them by reading RunState.cs three days ago, nothing in this round touched Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs, and re-grading eight criteria I have no new information about would be duplicated cost dressed as diligence. I say so rather than implying a fuller review than I performed. Criterion 6 moves out of unsatisfiableAsWritten because the specification defect that put it there has been cured by its author on RUL-0001's terms (matter 5); it is graded satisfiedByEvidence because the rewritten Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote pins the amended boundary and ran green in EVD-0011. I record explicitly that I did NOT carry unsatisfiableAsWritten forward as a formality: the criterion is now true, and leaving it graded unsatisfiable would misdescribe a cured defect as a live one. Criteria 7 and 11 are graded satisfiedByEvidence on EVD-0010 and EVD-0011 respectively; both are what RUL-0001 asked for and neither existed when RUL-0001 was written. Criterion 8 moves from satisfiedByInspection to notYetEvidenced, which is the one grade in this assessment that is HARSHER than RUL-0001's, and I want the reason on the record rather than inferred: its closing clause, 'No other existing assertion in this file is altered', is a claim about a diff. RUL-0001 read the file and reconciled test counts, then named the diff as a gate step someone with a shell must perform and stated it was not claiming it as done. Nobody performed it, nothing records it, and reading is not diffing -- qa-director's own phrase, applied here to qa-director's own order. Studio/build/check-forbidden-remedies.sh covers 'removed' mechanically and covers neither 'altered' nor 'weakened'. This is not a finding against the implementer, whose three replacements RUL-0001 examined in detail and found strictly stronger than what they replaced; it is an unperformed verification step, and it is the same one outstanding on WO-0009.

blockingConditions: NO GATE VERDICT EXISTS FOR WO-0008. Studio/kernel/schemas/gate.schema.json defines gate-verdict as a record keyed to a taskId, and no live instance of it exists anywhere in the studio -- the only occurrences of the string in the repository are the schema itself and four kernel fixtures. Until it exists, writing completedByGate 'G2' records that a gate ruled when what happened is that an agent reported one. G2's owner is 'ci' and its overridableBy is the empty array; this verdict is not mine to supply and not my dispatcher's to supply by reporting it.

NO RECORD TIES A GREEN BUILD-AND-SUITE RUN TO COMMIT 13900d3. EVD-0011 is at 4f4135e. The strings '13900d3' and 'run 58' appear nowhere in the repository. The evidence schema requires a commit for every automated tier because evidence that cannot be tied to a state of the code cannot be reasoned about later; closure as proposed would cite a commit the studio has no record of. Recording the gate verdict with its commit discharges this and the condition above together.

THE DIFF NAMED BY RUL-0001 MATTER 4 IS UNPERFORMED AND UNRECORDED: `git diff ae3169b -- Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateVerificationTests.cs`, confirming only the three founder-authorised hunks plus the added regression test. This is criterion 8's closing clause and is checkable no other way. check-forbidden-remedies.sh covers 'removed' but not 'altered' or 'weakened'. File the output as a T0 evidence record and cite it in the gate verdict.

Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote MUST BE RENAMED BEFORE THE GATE VERDICT IS TAKEN, per matter 4, to a name stating what it now pins rather than the opposite. Authorised by this ruling; the exact string is the implementing agent's, not mine. Blocking on timing rather than on correctness: the file leaves every open order's write scope the moment WO-0008 closes, and an authorisation that outlives its order produces the unattributed edit RUL-0004 objected to. If it slips past the verdict it is not to be made afterwards on the strength of this paragraph -- it returns to me.

boundariesObserved: I wrote no production code and no test code, and touched nothing under Assets/**, including the test I have ruled must be renamed -- that is dispatched, not performed, and I declined even to specify the new name because choosing a test's name is nearer to authoring a test than I am willing to come. I amended no acceptance criterion; I ratified an amendment its author had already made under RUL-0001's authorisation, and ratifying is not authoring. I left Studio/orders/open/WO-0008.json byte-for-byte untouched: I was authorised to write status, completedByGate and completedAt if the order was closable, it is not, and the correct action on a refusal is to leave the file exactly as I found it. I did not mark WO-0008 complete, did not sign G2, and did not treat a reported CI result as a gate verdict -- which is the substance of matter 2 and the whole reason this dispatch was worth making. I cleared and weakened none of RUL-0001's conditions; I found all four discharged on the tree and then ADDED one RUL-0001 had left in prose rather than in its blocking list, which is the direction a reviewing director should err in. I did not re-derive the eight criteria RUL-0001 graded by inspection and said so rather than implying I had. I did not edit Studio/build, the kernel, the constitution, CI, LESSONS.md or any proposal's status; where those need changing I named the change and its owner. I did not escalate to the founder: the founder asked for these orders to be closed, this ruling declines, and declining a founder's request on a matter inside my own authority is not an escalation -- it is the job. Nothing here touches the pillars, the non-goals, an irreversible action, monetisation or player data.
whyNoChallenge: No criterion of WO-0008 is violated by the implementation, and I checked before choosing an instrument. RUL-0001 found the code correct across every criterion it could reach, the two criteria it left unevidenced now carry evidence records, and the one specification defect it found has been amended by its author in the correct direction. The single grade I hardened -- criterion 8 to notYetEvidenced -- is unmet for want of a verification step nobody performed, not for want of correct code, and challenging an implementer because a director's named gate step went unrun would be manufactured. The gate-verdict gap that blocks closure is a hole in the studio's own process which I own, and filing a challenge against myself would be theatre where a ruling and a digest item are the honest instruments. The rename is a consequence of an authorisation my predecessor scoped narrowly, correctly obeyed by the agent, and is dispatched rather than challenged.
limitations: I have no shell, no git and no CI access in this environment; my instruments were file reading and search over the working tree. Four consequences, stated rather than glossed. First and most important: I could not verify that G2 CI run 58 exists, that it is green, or that commit 13900d3 exists or carries the work described to me. Neither string appears anywhere in the repository. I have not ruled that the claim is false -- I have ruled that I cannot check it and that transcribing an unverifiable gate result into a completion field is the self-certification the architecture forbids. If a gate-verdict record is produced, this limitation ceases to matter and so does my refusal. Second, I could not perform the diff in matter 3 for the same reason, which is why I made it a condition rather than clearing it. Third, my grading of criteria 1-5, 9, 10 and 12 is adopted from RUL-0001 and inherits whatever that reading was worth; I re-derived none of it, and RUL-0001 was itself produced without a shell. Fourth, the timestamps I relied on in RUL-0006 matter 3 -- for the sibling finding that no T1 record demonstrably covers a tree containing the RUL-0004-authorised amendment -- are the 'at' fields of the records themselves, and I have no independent clock; if those fields are nominal rather than captured, that particular observation weakens, though the missing gate verdict does not depend on it at all.
